items.response: The Treaty of Versailles, signed in 1919 after World War I, imposed harsh penalties on Germany and ended German involvement in World War II. It is often cited as a factor leading to the rise of extremist politics in Germany during the Cold War. However, it was not the only cause; rather, it exacerbated tensions between France and Germany that had been building for decades beforehand.
